evidence.summary: Riley says diverse people were assimilated, later disconnected when an electrokinetic storm disabled their cube, regained individual memories, and then fractured into conflict.
Voyager finds a dead Borg cube whose systems failed roughly five years earlier and recovers evidence consistent with catastrophic electro-mechanical damage.
Former Borg temporarily link Chakotay into a small controlled network that repairs his severe neural injuries and shares memories and feelings.
Chakotay reports hearing the linked members' thoughts as his own and retaining intimate knowledge from the connection after it ends.
The cooperative asks Voyager to reactivate the cube's neuroelectric generator so all former Borg on the planet can be permanently linked to suppress violence and build a cooperative society.
Janeway refuses because thousands would be forced into a collective without consent and because reactivating Borg systems creates unknown risks.
The cooperative remotely reestablishes a link with Chakotay against his will and compels him to reactivate the Borg generator.
After the planetwide link forms, the new cooperative destroys the reactivated cube and releases Chakotay.
The new cooperative admits forcing Chakotay but says it was necessary for survival; Janeway recognizes he acted against his will.
Chakotay remains troubled because the cooperative's ideals coexist with willingness to impose collective control when useful.

assertions.object: former Borg population after restored neural link

neutral_coding.plot_problem: Former Borg seek to use collective linkage as a cure for post-assimilation social violence and ultimately force Chakotay to help impose it.
neutral_coding.identity_memory: Regained individuality and later relinking are represented as neural/social states, not binary person replacement.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: The cooperative does save lives and destroy the Borg cube, but those outcomes do not erase its nonconsensual control of Chakotay and the wider population.
